items.title: Not Truly Multilingual: Script Consistency as a Missing Dimension in VLM Evaluation
items.authors: Prabhjot Singh, Bhushan Pawar, Madhu Reddiboina, Rajvee Sheth
items.description: This work exposes a critical blind spot in multilingual VLM evaluation: the 'One Language, One Script' assumption that overlooks billions of multi-script language users. Introducing PuMVR, a 1,000-instance benchmark spanning Punjabi's three active scripts (Gurmukhi, Shahmukhi, and Roman), we evaluate 10 state-of-the-art VLMs and uncover a systematic Script Gap, with accuracy deltas reaching 16% and Script Consistency Rate (SCR) falling as low as 24.8% on identical semantic content. Visual grounding boosts performance uniformly but never closes the gap, and cross-script in-context transfer proves highly brittle, exposing script-locked knowledge representations even in frontier models. Validated by McNemar tests across all script pairs, this study establishes SCR as a mandatory metric for script-agnostic evaluation and equitable multilingual AI.

items.title: When Less Is More: Simplicity Beats Complexity for Physics-Constrained InSAR Phase Unwrapping
items.venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters (Accepted August 2026) & ML4RS Workshop @ ICLR 2026 | Oral Presentation ⭐
items.description: This research challenges the trend of using high-complexity architectures for geophysical tasks, demonstrating that a vanilla U-Net outperforms larger attention-based models by 34% in R² and 51% in RMSE. By achieving a 2.5x speedup (2.92ms latency), the work provides a physics-grounded solution that preserves the smoothness of surface deformation while meeting sub-100ms requirements for operational early-warning systems.

items.title: FirstPass: Grounding AI Scientific Judgment in Multi-Round Editorial Outcomes
items.authors: Prabhjot Singh, Somnath Luitel, Manmeet Singh, Josh Durkee
items.venue: AI4Science Workshop @ ICML 2026 (Dual Acceptance: Research Track & Dataset Competition Track)
items.description: FirstPass is a novel AI system trained on 3,668 multi-round scientific dialogues to predict real-world editorial outcomes across five disciplines with 80.5% accuracy. By simulating expert critique before submission, it acts as an anticipatory co-author that identifies methodological weaknesses and reduces revision cycles. This work establishes response-only loss masking as a critical prerequisite for exercising genuine scientific judgment in long-context models.

items.title: The Hallucination Snowball: Modeling Error Propagation as State Transitions in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
items.venue: Failure Modes in Agentic AI Workshop @ ICML 2026
items.description: This paper formalizes the hallucination snowball effect, demonstrating how errors in multi-agent LLM pipelines transform from checkable facts into unrecoverable narratives. By modeling this propagation as a first-order Markov process, the research proves that implementing boundary gates at agent handoffs reduces hallucination survival from 58.4% to 16.2%. This work provides the first mathematical framework for propagation control, offering a scalable strategy to ensure reliability in high-stakes, sequential AI architectures.

items.title: Beyond 'One Language, One Script': Quantifying Orthographic Bias in Multilingual VLMs with PuMVR
items.authors: Prabhjot Singh, Bhushan Pawar, Madhu Reddiboina
items.description: This research introduces PuMVR, the first benchmark designed to quantify script-dependent bias in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) across Punjabi’s three active scripts. By exposing a significant "Script Gap" and reasoning divergence, the work challenges the prevailing "One Language, One Script" paradigm and establishes a new framework for orthographic equity. It provides a critical methodology for ensuring AI systems serve over a billion multi-script language users with consistent reliability and fidelity.

items.title: The Architecture Was Doing the Work: Why NLI Debiasing Results Do Not Generalise
items.venue: Workshop on Insights from Negative Results in NLP @ EMNLP 2026
items.description: Running 44 controlled experiments across eleven debiasing strategies, two architecturally distinct models, and two corpora, this work shows that NLI debiasing effectiveness is driven almost entirely by architecture rather than method. On ELECTRA-small, every debiasing intervention fails completely, statistically indistinguishable from the baseline on HANS, while the identical codebase produces real, if inconsistent, gains on RoBERTa-base. The paper traces this to a capacity failure rather than a pipeline artifact and further finds that the assumed robustness-accuracy tradeoff inverts on RoBERTa, arguing for cross-architecture validation, confidence intervals, and per-heuristic reporting as non-negotiable standards for future debiasing research.

items.title: Trustworthy AI for the Ocean: Bridging the Science-Policy Divide
items.authors: Arjun Pankajakshan, Joi Danielson, Zifu Wang, Prabhjot Singh, et al.
items.venue: npj Ocean Sustainability (Nature Portfolio) | Accepted March 2026
items.description: Developed IPOSGPT, a domain-specific Large Language Model (LLM) grounded in a curated corpus of over 800,000 ocean science and policy documents to provide decision-makers with verifiable, rapid insights. By implementing a hierarchical Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, the system achieved a 0% citation hallucination rate, significantly outperforming generalist models in evidence traceability and scientific grounding. The framework was successfully piloted with the Government of Seychelles, accelerating the assessment of circular economy strategies to combat marine plastic pollution.

items.title: Genius AI SaaS: A Unified Multi-Modal Content Generation Platform
items.authors: Prabhjot Singh, Srishti Sharma, Arjun Pankajakshan
items.description: Genius AI is a unified SaaS platform that integrates text, code, image, video, and music generation into a single, seamless web application. By orchestrating advanced AI models through a user-centric interface, it eliminates workflow fragmentation and empowers non-technical creators to significantly accelerate high-quality multimedia production.

items.title: Same Facts, Different Diagnosis: Measuring and Mitigating Narrative Anchoring in Clinical Language Models
items.authors: Prabhjot Singh, Pritam Deka, Vijay Chennareddy
items.description: This work identifies Narrative Anchoring: a bias where clinical language models shift their diagnostic output based on a patient's sociolinguistic register alone, with no demographic marker ever stated. We introduce NarrativeShield-SDoH, a dataset of 1,000 USMLE clinical vignettes rewritten into three register-distinct personas under an independently audited fact-preservation guarantee. Across seven language models, Narrative Anchoring is statistically significant under direct prompting in every model tested, and chain-of-thought or explicit debiasing instructions mitigate it only partially. We propose NarrativeShield, a three-agent pipeline that structurally extracts and verifies clinical facts before diagnostic reasoning begins, reducing the Narrative Anchoring Gap to near-zero and achieving the most stable diagnostic decisions of any method tested, establishing that structural separation of narrative from clinical fact is key to equitable clinical AI.

items.title: Talking a Rejection Into an Accept: How Confidence Framing Fools (Some) LLM Reviewers
items.authors: Prabhjot Singh, Somnath Luitel, Manmeet Singh
items.venue: Under Review | NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI-Native Academia: Authorship, Peer Review, and Conference Governance under AI
items.description: This work tests whether AI-generated peer review is uniformly vulnerable to style manipulation or only in specific models, evaluating 9 open-weight reviewer models on 100 real ICLR 2026 and ICML 2026 abstracts rewritten into five controlled confidence tones with every factual claim held fixed. Hedging is punished in all 9 of 9 models, the only effect that replicates without exception, while overclaiming splits models in opposite directions, from severe penalties to significant rewards. Confidence reframing flips a genuine rejection into an accept in up to 35.7% of eligible cases, but only in 2 of 9 models with adequate sample size, while which reviewer model is deployed explains more variance in a paper's score than any style manipulation tested, arguing that model-selection auditing, not blanket AI-reviewer distrust, is the actionable lever for venues already deploying these systems.

items.title: The Trust Gap: LLM Judges Are Consistent, Not Correct
items.venue: Under Review | NeurIPS 2026 Workshop "Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development"
items.description: This work audits whether trusting an LLM judge because it agrees with itself is a safe substitute for checking whether it agrees with reality, testing six independently built judges on 200 real coding-agent trajectories validated against executable outcomes. Every one of the six judges is substantially less accurate against ground truth on trajectories whose surface features are atypical for their outcome, with unanimous accuracy drops of 18 to 42 percentage points, while self-consistency across repeated queries on the same trajectories barely moves, holding significantly for only one of six judges. This validity-reliability dissociation shows self-consistency is not a usable proxy for correctness, and a simple disagreement-triggered escalation-to-human-review protocol recovers 84.9% accuracy on the trajectories it accepts, turning the diagnosis into a practical, low-cost mitigation for teams building agent verification pipelines.

items.title: When Retrieval Helps and Distracts: Evaluating Evidence-Generating LLMs for Biomedical Claim Verification
items.description: This work presents a systematic evaluation of evidence-generating LLMs for biomedical claim verification on CARE-XAI, a unified benchmark spanning five biomedical and health fact-checking sources. Comparing base LLMs, PubMed retrieval-augmented LLMs, fine-tuned LLMs, and biomedical encoder classifiers under a shared protocol, we find biomedical classifiers remain strongest for verdict-only prediction while fine-tuned LLMs are the strongest evidence-generating systems. We introduce Bio-GRACE, a gold-reference-normalized diagnostic showing that PubMed retrieval helps PubMed-aligned sources like PubMedQA and SciFact but distracts models on broader public-health claims, motivating selective rather than always-on retrieval for biomedical fact-checking.
